, The Court
Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. The insurer is in appeal challenging the award of Rs.20,94,000/- for the death of Narayanamma,
a poura karmika, aged about 51 years.

2. The principal contention advanced by the insurer is that, the Tribunal has deducted 1/3rd of the income and ought to have been deducted 50% of the income since the deceased had left behind her husband and two major sons.
It is also contended that the rate of interest awarded at 8% p.a. would be improper.
3. The argument of the insurer that the deceased would have spent 50% of her income for herself since both of her children were majors, cannot be accepted.
It is to be noted here that the deceased was a poura karmika and having regard to her nature of work, the expectation that she would spend 50% of her income, cannot be accepted.

Therefore, I am of the view, that the deduction of 1/3rd by the Tribunal, in this particular case cannot be found fault with.

The amount in deposit, if any,
